Skills
Azure (VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure AD / Entra ID, Azure Monitor), Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL), PowerShell, Bash, Terraform, Bicep, Azure DevOps Pipelines, Docker, Kubernetes (AKS), Ansible, Active Directory, Microsoft 365 administration, networking (TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls)

Experience

Cloud Engineer (contract) - Havenstad Logistics B.V., Rotterdam
Mar 2025 - Present

- Led the move of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS in 2019 (lift and shift).

Certifications
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104), 2019
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (003), 2025

Languages
Dutch (native), English (fluent), Twi (spoken)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clean, concise, credible, and easy to scan. It presents relevant Azure, Terraform, networking, Linux, virtual-machine, Kubernetes, and automation experience with useful scale indicators such as 400 VMs, 12 AKS clusters, 15 applications, and 60 migrated servers. The main content weakness is that it undersells the strongest evidence in the candidate material: landing-zone architecture, private endpoints and DNS, Terratest, drift detection, Azure Migrate, deployment-frequency improvement, and the no-unplanned-downtime migration result. There is also no Professional Summary or dedicated project detail, so the document does not clearly position the candidate for infrastructure design and platform ownership. Technical leadership and stakeholder engagement are only indirectly demonstrated.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses ATS-friendly plain text headings, conventional chronology, standard job titles, and searchable technology keywords. It should parse reliably because it has no tables, columns, graphics, or unusual formatting. ATS coverage is weaker for this specific vacancy because the CV does not explicitly use supported terms such as cloud infrastructure design, cloud operations, infrastructure as code, landing zone, system architecture, private endpoints, private DNS, Azure Migrate, observability, reliability, or technical leadership. Terraform is present, but Terragrunt is not supported by the candidate information and must not be added. AI screening probability is moderate to good for an Azure infrastructure role, but only moderate for this exact vacancy because the CV does not demonstrate mTLS/SSL/TLS, Terragrunt, AWS, IoT or remote-device integration, or explicit stakeholder-facing technical proposals.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is hands-on infrastructure engineering and cloud design/operations in Azure, including a large estate, Terraform networking modules, AKS operations, Azure DevOps pipelines, Windows and Linux administration, virtual machines, and practical security controls. The Azure landing-zone work is relevant to the job's architecture, networking, reliability, and ownership focus. The candidate's experience leading the VMware-to-Azure migration also supports technical leadership. The document does not show mTLS or SSL/TLS, Terragrunt, AWS, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, or JVM/backend development. The candidate material also does not establish direct experience agreeing interfaces with external manufacturers or leading stakeholder proposals from idea to production. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than CV-writing defects. The current CV could nevertheless make the supported architecture, security, automation, and leadership evidence much more visible.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the CV, insert a 3–4 line Professional Summary directly below the contact details. Make it accurately state the candidate’s hands-on Azure infrastructure engineering and operations experience, Terraform-based cloud design, landing-zone networking, AKS, Azure DevOps automation, Windows/Linux administration, and experience leading a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration. Use terms such as “cloud infrastructure design,” “cloud operations,” “infrastructure as code,” “networking,” and “technical leadership” only in connection with the documented experience.

2. In the Skills section, reorganize the skills into ATS-readable categories rather than one long list. For example: “Cloud: Azure VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure AD/Entra ID, Azure Monitor”; “Infrastructure as Code: Terraform, Bicep”; “CI/CD and Containers: Azure DevOps YAML Pipelines, Docker, Kubernetes/AKS”; “Systems: Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL), Active Directory, Microsoft 365”; “Networking and Security: TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls, private endpoints, MFA, conditional access”; and “Automation: PowerShell, Bash, Ansible.” Add “private endpoints” and “Azure Monitor” because they are supported by the candidate material and already partly present in the CV. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, AWS, or other unsupported technologies.

3. In the Experience section under “Cloud Engineer (contract) – Havenstad Logistics B.V.,” expand the Terraform bullet to show the architecture scope from the portfolio: “Designed and implemented hub-spoke landing-zone networking in Terraform across 3 Azure subscriptions, including Azure Firewall, VNet peering, private DNS zones, and private endpoints for storage and SQL.” This is substantially more aligned with cloud environment design, system architecture, and networking than the current shorter wording.

4. Under the same Havenstad role, add the supported testing and operations detail from the portfolio: “Added Terratest module tests to the Azure DevOps pipeline and implemented a nightly infrastructure-drift detection job.” This demonstrates infrastructure quality, operational discipline, and analytical engineering. Keep the wording limited to Terratest; do not imply general Go development.

5. Replace or expand the Azure DevOps bullet under Havenstad with the measurable portfolio result: “Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines covering build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS, increasing deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.” This better demonstrates platform enablement and support for deployable, maintainable services.

6. In the Havenstad role, add one concise AKS operations bullet if space permits: “Operate 12 AKS clusters across 3 Azure subscriptions, including cluster upgrades, node-pool management, and ingress operations; application manifests remain owned by development teams.” This accurately clarifies the candidate’s Kubernetes responsibility without overstating application ownership.

7. In the Experience section under “Systems Administrator – Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services,” replace the migration bullet with the stronger documented result: “Planned and led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate, Azure VMs, VNets, site-to-site VPN, and PowerShell; completed cutovers over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.” This makes the cloud design, systems operation, leadership, networking, and reliability evidence immediately visible.

8. Under the same Systems Administrator role, revise the automation and escalation bullets to use the job’s supported language: “Automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell” and “Served as second-line escalation for network and Active Directory issues.” If accurate based on the existing material, add a short phrase that the role involved diagnosing infrastructure issues and coordinating resolution; do not claim formal stakeholder management that is not documented.

9. Add a compact “Selected Infrastructure Projects” section between Experience and Education, using the documented projects only. Include “Azure Landing Zone Networking,” “Release Pipelines for Internal Apps,” and “VMware to Azure Migration,” each with one or two outcome-focused bullets. This is preferable to leaving the strongest architecture and delivery evidence implicit in the employment bullets.

10. In the Skills or Summary section, use “Azure Monitor” and, where supported by the candidate’s existing skill listing, describe the platform as observable and monitored. Do not claim specific observability dashboards, alerting ownership, or reliability metrics beyond what the candidate has documented.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, professionally structured, and easy to scan. It presents strong evidence of Azure operations, Terraform-based infrastructure, Azure DevOps automation, Linux, Windows, virtual machines, and practical security work. The quantified scope is particularly effective: approximately 400 VMs, 12 AKS clusters, 15 application pipelines, 250 servers, and 60 migrated servers. Its main content weakness is that it undersells the strongest project-level evidence in the candidate information, including private DNS, VNet peering, Azure Migrate, Terratest, drift detection, Helm, deployment-frequency improvement, and the no-unplanned-downtime migration outcome. It also does not explicitly demonstrate systems design or stakeholder engagement, although the source material supports stronger wording for infrastructure design and technical leadership.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience, readable text, and ATS-friendly keyword formatting. It should parse reliably and has a good baseline AI-screening probability for Azure-focused infrastructure roles. Screening probability is reduced for this specific vacancy because the document does not contain the exact terms Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, systems architecture, system design, stakeholder engagement, or observability. Terragrunt, mTLS, and SSL/TLS should not be added because they are not supported by the original candidate information. The most useful ATS improvement is to expand existing truthful experience with terms such as infrastructure design, landing-zone architecture, Azure IaaS, Azure Migrate, private DNS, VNet peering, infrastructure as code, deployment automation, monitoring, and security baselines. There are no obvious formatting defects or hallucinated technologies in the document.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: This is a credible match for the hands-on cloud infrastructure and operations aspects of the role, particularly Azure platform operation, Terraform, networking, Kubernetes/AKS, Linux, virtual machines, migration, automation, and practical security. The candidate's Azure experience is relevant because the advertisement accepts other major clouds, but there is no AWS experience. The document does not establish Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, backend/full-stack development, or direct experience agreeing interfaces with external manufacturers. The candidate information supports stronger evidence of landing-zone architecture, technical leadership, and reliable delivery through the 60-server migration and the Azure networking project, but it does not provide evidence of stakeholder management, telemetry, train connectivity, certificate management, or system observability beyond the listed Azure Monitor skill. These are substantive experience gaps or evidence gaps, not problems that can be solved by inventing keywords.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Experience section under “Cloud Engineer (contract) - Havenstad Logistics B.V.”, expand the landing-zone bullet using only the portfolio evidence: “Designed and implemented a Terraform-based Azure landing-zone network across 3 subscriptions, including hub-spoke VNets, VNet peering, Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, and private endpoints for Storage and SQL.” This makes the systems design and network architecture contribution much clearer.
2. In the same Havenstad experience entry, add a factual bullet: “Added Terratest module tests and a nightly Terraform drift-detection job to the Azure DevOps pipeline.” This improves evidence of infrastructure quality and operational reliability without claiming Terragrunt experience.
3. In the same Havenstad experience entry, strengthen the pipeline bullet to: “Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines, deploying to App Service or AKS; increased deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.” This adds supported backend-context, deployment automation, and measurable impact.
4. In the Systems Administrator experience entry, replace “Led the move of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS in 2019 (lift and shift)” with “Planned and led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate; completed cutover over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.” This better demonstrates technical leadership, cloud design and operations, virtual-machine experience, and delivery reliability.
5. In the Skills section, change the networking entry to include the supported technologies “private DNS, VNet peering, site-to-site VPN, and Azure Firewall” alongside TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, and firewalls. Do not add mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, or Terragrunt because they are not supported by the candidate information.
6. In the Professional Summary, consider replacing the final phrase “practical security baselines” with “Azure landing-zone networking, infrastructure as code, migration, deployment automation, and practical security baselines.” This remains truthful while aligning more directly with the role's infrastructure engineering and cloud design language.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, professional, well-structured CV with a strong recent Azure infrastructure profile. The quantified scope is persuasive: approximately 400 VMs, 12 AKS clusters, three subscriptions, 15 applications, and a 60-server migration completed without unplanned downtime. The recent experience is appropriately placed first and the two-sentence summary is concise. The main content weakness is that several relevant portfolio details are absent, while some of the role's central requirements—Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS, stakeholder leadership, and broader systems architecture—are not evidenced. The document also does not explicitly show the candidate's ownership of AKS operations, Terraform testing, or drift detection, despite those being relevant and supported by the candidate material.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly conventional headings, plain text formatting, reverse-chronological experience, readable dates, and strong Azure/Terraform/DevOps keywords. It should parse well and has a good AI-screening probability for Azure-focused infrastructure roles. ATS alignment would improve by adding supported terms such as Azure landing zone, infrastructure as code, Terratest, Terraform drift detection, Azure Migrate, site-to-site VPN, private endpoints, Helm, certificate-related terminology only if genuinely supported, and platform observability. The principal ATS limitation is that the job specifically requests Terragrunt and mTLS/SSL/TLS, neither of which is supported by the candidate information and therefore should not be added. The skills line is dense but still parseable; grouping skills into categories would improve scanability without changing the content.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document strongly demonstrates hands-on infrastructure engineering, Azure cloud design and operations, Terraform, Linux, virtual machines, networking, security baselines, and deployment automation. It is a credible match where the employer accepts Azure as an alternative to AWS. The landing-zone work, multi-subscription network design, Azure DevOps automation, AKS operations, and VMware-to-Azure migration are particularly relevant to an engineering-led platform role. However, the candidate has no AWS experience, no Terragrunt experience, no stated mTLS or SSL/TLS experience, and no IoT, automotive, or remote-device integration experience. The material also does not clearly establish broader systems architecture, stakeholder engagement, or leading technical proposals from idea to production. These are candidate-background gaps or partial gaps rather than defects that can be solved by inventing experience. The CV can nevertheless present the supported cloud-design, technical leadership, operational ownership, and analytical evidence more effectively.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE CONTENT IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the Experience section under “Cloud Engineer (contract) - Havenstad Logistics B.V.”, add a bullet based on the supported candidate material: “Operate 12 AKS clusters, including upgrades, node-pool management, and ingress operations, while application manifests remain owned by development teams.” This makes the operational ownership relevant to the requirement to build and operate reliable platforms without overstating application-development responsibility.
2. In the same Havenstad experience entry, revise the existing Terraform bullet to include the supported testing and maintainability work: “Designed and implemented Terraform modules for an Azure landing-zone network across three subscriptions, including hub-spoke VNets, VNet peering, Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, and private endpoints for Storage and SQL; added Terratest module tests and nightly Terraform drift detection in Azure DevOps.” This more directly demonstrates infrastructure-as-code quality and operational discipline.
3. In the same Havenstad entry, revise the Azure DevOps bullet to include the supported deployment scope and measurable outcome: “Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines covering build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS; increased deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.”
4. In the Skills section, reorganize the current single dense list into ATS-readable categories: “Cloud: Azure (VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure Monitor, Azure AD / Entra ID); Infrastructure as Code: Terraform, Bicep, Terratest; CI/CD: Azure DevOps YAML Pipelines; Containers: Docker, Kubernetes, AKS, Helm; Systems: Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL), Windows Server, Active Directory, Microsoft 365; Automation: PowerShell, Bash, Ansible; Networking: TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, site-to-site VPN, firewalls, Azure Firewall, private DNS, VNet peering, private endpoints.” Add only the supported terms listed here.
5. In the Systems Administrator experience entry, revise “Led the move of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS in 2019” to: “Planned and led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate; completed cutover over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.” This provides stronger evidence of cloud design, migration planning, technical leadership, and reliability.
6. In the Professional Summary, retain the two-sentence limit but make the design and operational scope more explicit. For example: “Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer with hands-on experience designing and operating Azure environments, building Terraform-based landing-zone networking, and automating application deployments with Azure DevOps. Experienced with Linux and Windows administration, AKS operations, infrastructure-as-code testing, Azure migration, and practical security baselines.” This uses supported evidence and avoids claiming AWS, Terragrunt, mTLS, or unsupported stakeholder leadership.
7. Do not add “Terragrunt,” “mTLS,” “SSL/TLS,” AWS, IoT, automotive integration, or certificate management anywhere in the CV unless the candidate can substantiate that experience. The candidate information explicitly states no AWS experience and provides no evidence for the other technologies.

MINOR ATS / COMPLETENESS IMPROVEMENTS
8. Add the supported “Azure Migrate,” “Helm,” and “Terratest” terms to the Skills section or relevant project-style bullets, because they are present in the candidate portfolio but currently absent from the document.
9. In the Freelance IT Administrator entry, revise the security bullet to: “Implemented repeatable Microsoft 365 security baselines for small-business clients, including MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing, backups, and a supporting PowerShell script and checklist.” This is more concrete and better supports practical security awareness.
10. If space permits, add a compact “Selected Projects” section after Experience containing the Azure Landing Zone Networking, Release Pipelines, and VMware-to-Azure Migration projects from the candidate portfolio. Do not duplicate every experience bullet; use it only to expose supported keywords such as Terratest, Azure Migrate, Helm, site-to-site VPN, and drift detection that are otherwise easy for an ATS or recruiter to miss.
